sourceText: Do B-e165 now. Is a mature lockfile library the better approach, and does it work cross-platform (Mac and Windows)? — maintainer, then approved the unified design: cross-platform proper-lockfile + content-bound verifyBuildBinding skip + a packages/utils binding across the three build call sites, and accepted adding the proper-lockfile dependency.
normalizedOutcome: Concurrent builds in one shared worktree no longer corrupt dist (no ENOTEMPTY / TS2307 / MODULE_NOT_FOUND under concurrent npm test): a live long-running build is never age-stolen from its lock, a dead holder is reclaimed race-free, and a build skips only when a content-hash binding proves dist matches source (never by mtime or by mere existence).
acceptanceClaim: The build critical section holds a cross-platform proper-lockfile mutex, and every build skip is gated by verifyBuildBinding (sha256 over all packages/main src+config and all dist, plus an analogous packages/utils binding), applied to the three build call sites (scripts/ensure-dist.mjs, scripts/build-main-with-binding.mjs which is the packages-main-build validate command, and the packages/utils build) — so concurrent npm tests never race into dist corruption and a stale/partial/orphaned dist is never reused.
